common_name: Gladiator Allium (Tall Classic Purple Ornamental Onion)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall, 6-8 inches deep, in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Gladiator is a tall, classic purple allium reliably perennializing better than some newer hybrid alliums.

directions: Plant bulbs 6-8 inches deep in fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Gladiator produces tall, sturdy stems topped with dense, perfectly spherical lavender-purple flower globes in late spring, one of the classic, most reliable ornamental onions for a mixed perennial border, standing taller than Purple Sensation but slightly smaller-headed than Globemaster. Bees are drawn to the flowers in large numbers, and the dried seed heads persist for weeks, providing architectural interest through summer if left standing. Plant lower, later-emerging perennials in front to mask the strap-like foliage, which yellows and dies back before or during bloom, a normal habit for ornamental alliums.

common_name: Millenium Allium (Compact Perennial Plant of the Year Ornamental Onion)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Millenium was named the Perennial Plant Association's Perennial Plant of the Year in 2018 for its clump-forming, non-invasive habit.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Millenium forms a neat, glossy, grass-like clump of foliage topped in mid-to-late summer by rounded, rose-purple flower globes, blooming later than most spring ornamental onions and filling a useful gap in the summer garden while drawing heavy bee and butterfly traffic. Unlike many alliums grown from bulbs, Millenium is a clump-forming perennial that stays put rather than spreading or self-seeding aggressively, making it a well-behaved choice for a mixed border, edging, or mass planting. It is drought-tolerant once established and rarely needs division, though congested clumps can be split in spring every several years to maintain vigor.
sources: Perennial Plant Association — Perennial Plant of the Year

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall, 3-4 inches deep, in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Schubertii produces one of the most dramatic, irregular firework-shaped flower heads of any ornamental onion.

directions: Plant bulbs 3-4 inches deep in fall in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; excellent drainage is essential, since this species is prone to bulb rot in wet conditions. Schubertii produces one of the most striking and unusual flower heads of any ornamental onion, a loose, irregular sphere of pale pink-purple florets held on stalks of dramatically varying length, giving each flower head an explosive, firework-like or dandelion-seed-head appearance up to a foot across on a relatively short plant. The dried seed heads are prized for everlasting arrangements and hold their sculptural form for months. Plant lower companion perennials in front to mask the strap-like foliage, which yellows and dies back before or during bloom, a normal habit for ornamental alliums.
